claims.claim: Aliskiren, a peptidomimetic renin inhibitor with a hydroxyethylene isostere, high molecular weight, and multiple H-bond donors/acceptors, has human oral bioavailability of only 2.6–5%, providing a transferable low-F precedent for the query's similar peptidomimetic scaffold.

Octreotide and GHRP-6, peptide-based molecules, show very low oral bioavailability (~0.3–0.6% and ~0.3%, respectively) in humans, supporting that peptide-like backbones with high polar surface area are poorly orally bioavailable.
SRT2104, a thiazole-containing small molecule, has absolute oral bioavailability of 13.8% in humans, below the 20% threshold, and shares thiazole/amide features with the query.
